edits.text: 语 is the standardized simplified form of 語, meaning “language” or “words” and associated with speaking. In 語, 言 contributes a speech-related meaning and 吾 serves as a sound element; in 语, 言 is written 讠. [E3, E4, E8, X-d5da1a9057cb74a11614]

The traditional graph 語 is phonosemantic: 言 contributes a speech-related meaning, while 吾 supplies a sound cue. In simplified 语, 言 is written 讠 in left-side position. Early bronze forms are reported with differing phonetic shapes, including one resembling a complex 五; that shape’s identity and pronunciation are unresolved. [E8, X-6c335e5b9fa63e22cca0, X-d5da1a9057cb74a11614, X-5efe188f2b8967ae03eb, X-91cfe3d10f114d0e34da, X-c0b6a4a6a83d0854d848]
讠 is the standardized simplified left-side form of 言 in 语. It carries the speech-related meaning attributed to 言 in traditional 語, without supplying a sound cue here. [E8, X-d5da1a9057cb74a11614]

吾 is identified as the phonetic element in traditional 語. Early bronze forms are also reported with a different phonetic shape resembling a complex 五, whose identity and relation to 吾 are unresolved. [E8, X-6c335e5b9fa63e22cca0, X-5efe188f2b8967ae03eb, X-c0b6a4a6a83d0854d848]

In the Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstructions, the readings are similar enough to support a proposed historical sound relationship. These are reconstructed forms, not recorded ancient pronunciations. [E9, X-e3af6124177b052533bf, X-5efe188f2b8967ae03eb]
The reconstructed Middle Chinese readings retain a comparison, though the forms differ. [X-e3af6124177b052533bf, X-5efe188f2b8967ae03eb]
The modern Mandarin readings differ and do not by themselves demonstrate the historical relationship. [E5, E12, X-5efe188f2b8967ae03eb]

The received traditional analysis writes 語 with 言 and 吾. A graphic-history account reports bronze examples with two phonetic shapes: one resembling a complex 五 and another identified as 吾. From Warring States script onward, it analyzes the form as 言 plus 吾. The curated seal-style drawings show 言 and 吾 separately in modern redrawings, not 語 or its early inscription forms. [E8, X-6c335e5b9fa63e22cca0, X-c0b6a4a6a83d0854d848, X-993bd5c69644d9132cec, X-0721549e53dac6f620e5]
In standardized simplified 语, 言 is written 讠 in left-side position. [E3, X-d5da1a9057cb74a11614]

The reported early bronze phonetic shape resembling a complex 五 has no established identity or pronunciation. The later analysis of 吾 and its sound comparison do not settle those questions. [X-6c335e5b9fa63e22cca0, X-5efe188f2b8967ae03eb, X-c0b6a4a6a83d0854d848]
A secondary proposal derives 言 from 語 with a nominal suffix, but its supporting discussion was not independently inspected, so the proposal remains unconfirmed. [E9, X-91cfe3d10f114d0e34da]

An Analects passage uses 語 for speaking or discussing. The surviving witness is not dated here, so the example does not establish the earliest attested use. [X-54c077aa35264a3b494e, X-f0406cd650ab46caf66f]
A separate Analects passage uses 語 for telling or addressing. Its chronological relation to the speak-or-discuss use is unresolved. [X-54c077aa35264a3b494e, X-f0406cd650ab46caf66f]

Current dictionary meanings include language, words, saying, and expression. The evidence does not establish when these uses developed in relation to the cited speak-or-discuss and tell uses. [E4, E11, X-f0406cd650ab46caf66f]
Other recorded senses include literary wording, signals, and animal calls, but no dated sequence links them to the speak-or-discuss, tell, or current meanings. [X-f0406cd650ab46caf66f]

The surviving witnesses behind the cited historical examples are undated here, and no chronology connecting those uses to current meanings is established. [X-54c077aa35264a3b494e, X-f0406cd650ab46caf66f]

语 means “language” or “words” and is associated with speaking. It is the simplified form of 語: 言 is written 讠, while 吾 is the sound element in the traditional graph. [E3, E4, E8, X-d5da1a9057cb74a11614]
讠 is the simplified left-side form of 言, which contributes speech-related meaning in traditional 語. [E8, X-d5da1a9057cb74a11614]
吾 is the sound element in traditional 語. Its older reconstructed reading is similar to 語’s, though their modern Mandarin readings differ. [E8, X-e3af6124177b052533bf, X-5efe188f2b8967ae03eb]
In simplified 语, 讠 is the standardized left-side form of 言 and carries its speech-related contribution; traditional 語 is analyzed with 言 in this position. [E8, X-d5da1a9057cb74a11614]

The received analysis identifies 吾 as the sound element in 語. Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstructions for 吾 (*ŋˤa) and 語 (*ŋ(r)aʔ) are similar enough to support a historical phonetic relation, despite their differing notation and modern Mandarin readings. A separate early bronze shape resembling a complex 五 is reported, but its identity and relation to 吾 remain unresolved. [E8, X-6c335e5b9fa63e22cca0, X-e3af6124177b052533bf, X-5efe188f2b8967ae03eb, X-c0b6a4a6a83d0854d848]
语 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 語; in left-side position, the 言 radical is written 讠 under the simplification rule. [E3, X-d5da1a9057cb74a11614]

An Analects passage uses 語 for speaking or discussing. The surviving witness is not dated here, so the example does not establish the earliest attested use. [X-54c077aa35264a3b494e, X-f0406cd650ab46caf66f]
A separate Analects passage uses 語 for telling or addressing. Its chronological relation to the speak-or-discuss use is unresolved. [X-54c077aa35264a3b494e, X-f0406cd650ab46caf66f]

Current dictionary meanings include language, words, saying, and expression. The evidence does not establish when these uses developed in relation to the cited speak-or-discuss and tell uses. [E4, E11, X-f0406cd650ab46caf66f]
